root_causes.root_cause: _word_has_reversed_morphology (helpers.py:1232) min word length raised from 2 to 4 chars by RFC-034 D7, combined with _arabic_readability_score returning 0 for garbled/fragmented Arabic text (no common-word matches), makes _tree_is_rtl_reversed and _check_bidi_coherence gates ineffective for سياسة حوكمة's garbling pattern. Short reversed Arabic words (2-3 chars) are skipped, and readability score comparisons produce 0==0 (no difference detected). Meanwhile _is_garbled_blob's single-letter fragment check (line 910-920) should be the backstop but the stored text likely has multi-char reversed words (not literal single-char tokens), bypassing the >40% single-char ratio threshold. validate_tree returns (True,'') and classify_verdict stores PASS despite 79-100% of nodes being garbled.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Lower _word_has_reversed_morphology min word length from 4 to 3, or add a dedicated garble gate prong in validate_tree that detects the specific pattern: per-node Arabic text where >50% of words have zero forward joins (indicating character-level reversal or fragmentation) even when they don't individually trigger _is_garbled_blob. Also thread expected_script from filename into classify_verdict's _garble_ratio call (line 1695 hardcodes None) so the Latin-gibberish prong in _is_garbled_blob can fire. RFC-034 D21 already identifies this classify_verdict expected_script=None gap.

root_causes.root_cause: classify_verdict depth threshold is a binary check (depth >= 2 -> eligible for PASS) with no document-complexity awareness. Haftpflicht-Allgemeine-Bedingungen has depth=2 and 136 nodes, which meets the code threshold, but the tree is structurally inadequate for a deeply structured German insurance document (should have Bedingungen/Abschnitt/Paragraf hierarchy). The Run 16 PASS was an LLM judge reclassification (watermark false-positive); Run 18's MARGINAL reflects the LLM judge being stricter about depth adequacy. The automated stored verdict is likely PASS or MARGINAL-from-leaf-concentration (if max_leaf_ratio > 0.30), not MARGINAL-from-depth. No code change caused this regression -- it is LLM judge scoring inconsistency surfacing a pre-existing classify_verdict threshold gap.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a document-complexity-aware depth check: for documents with high node counts (e.g., >50 nodes), require depth >= 3 or depth proportional to log(node_count) for PASS eligibility. Alternatively, introduce a depth_adequacy_ratio metric (depth / expected_depth based on content_class or node_count) as a PASS criterion alongside the existing binary threshold.
